title: The City Seen from Both Sides

paragraphs.en: A city can look orderly on a planning map and confusing from the street. When a local research team followed a bus line through a neglected area, it discovered that the official picture did not describe everyday life. A road ran between an industrial site and a crowded housing estate, but residents could not cross it safely. The nearest bridge was far away. A mother taking her child to school had to go around the factory instead of walking across the road. The journey was short on paper and exhausting in practice, especially without a car.
paragraphs.zh: 城市在规划图上可能井然有序，从街头看却令人困惑。当地研究团队沿公交线路走进一个长期被忽视的地区，发现官方图景无法描述日常生活。一条公路位于工业用地和拥挤住宅区之间，居民却不能安全穿越。最近的桥很远。一位母亲送孩子上学时，必须绕过工厂，而不能直接横穿公路。地图上距离很短，实际走起来却很累，尤其是没有汽车的人。

paragraphs.en: The team began at the center and moved toward the south of the city. Along the river, expensive apartments rose above an old market. Near the market, shopkeepers stored goods under temporary roofs, while signs advertising foreign investment appeared over the entrance to a new office block. Here, economic growth was visible, but its benefits were uneven. People living below the railway embankment had poor access to clean public space. Those on the other side enjoyed a park within walking distance. A person's position in the city shaped opportunities as powerfully as their income did.
paragraphs.zh: 团队从市中心出发，向南走。沿河，高档公寓耸立在老市场上方。市场附近，店主把货物放在临时棚顶下，而新办公楼入口上方挂着宣传外国投资的标牌。这里的经济增长清晰可见，但收益分配不均。住在铁路路基下方的人很难使用干净的公共空间，另一侧的居民却能步行到公园。一个人在城市中的位置，对机会的影响几乎同收入一样大。

paragraphs.en: In the middle of the district, residents gathered outside a library to discuss the situation. Some argued against any new construction; others wanted development, provided that it created a better place to live. A retired teacher asked where the younger generation would go if every affordable building disappeared. A shop owner pointed down the street to a vacant lot and suggested a shared garden. Land had become an investment before it was treated as a home. The discussion revealed a conflict found throughout the country: protecting existing communities while making room for a growing urban population.
paragraphs.zh: 在这一地区的中部，居民聚集到图书馆外讨论现状。有些人反对任何新建设，也有人支持发展，前提是它能创造更好的居住环境。一位退休教师问，如果所有负担得起的房屋都消失，年轻人还能住在哪里。店主指着街道下方的空地，建议建设共享花园。土地首先被视为投资对象，而不是家园。这场讨论揭示了全国常见的矛盾：既要保护现有社区，也要为不断增长的城市人口腾出空间。

paragraphs.en: An international consultant offered examples from another nation, but warned that a successful project could not simply be copied. Each town had its own history, and each region faced different constraints. The state could set standards, yet decisions about a particular neighborhood depended upon detailed knowledge of its people. Among the proposed measures were lower speed limits, a crossing near the school, and a public seating area at the top of the hill. These were modest interventions. Nevertheless, they addressed the daily barriers that large redevelopment schemes often missed when viewed from a distance.
paragraphs.zh: 一位国际顾问介绍了另一个国家的案例，但提醒大家不能直接复制成功项目。每座城镇都有自己的历史，每个地区面对的限制也不同。国家可以制定标准，但具体社区的决策必须建立在对居民的细致了解上。提议包括限速、学校附近的人行过街设施以及山顶的公共座椅。这些措施规模不大，却针对了大型改造方案在远处观察时常常忽略的日常障碍。

paragraphs.en: At the final stage of the survey, students marked unsafe ground and photographed broken steps. They recorded places where a wheelchair user would be forced off the pavement and routes that became inaccessible after dark. Their report went beyond complaints by proposing changes that officials could inspect and evaluate. It did not promise to solve every urban problem. Instead, it argued that good planning begins with a simple test: whether people can reach the things they need. A city is more than the outline of its buildings. It is the practical freedom to move, meet, rest, and belong.
paragraphs.zh: 调查最后阶段，学生标出不安全的地面，拍摄破损台阶。他们记录轮椅使用者不得不离开人行道的地点，以及天黑后难以通行的路线。报告并不止于抱怨，而是提出官员能够实地检查和评估的改变。它没有承诺解决所有城市问题，而是认为良好规划应从一个简单检验开始：人们是否能到达自己需要的地方。城市不只是建筑的轮廓，还意味着移动、相聚、休息和获得归属感的实际自由。
